answer.rationale: Memory 57 is relatively strong because it explicitly reports qualified revenue with no measurable retention harm, though it is limited to established customers and does not establish long-term durability. Memory 44 directly supports qualified revenue through higher-quality enterprise pipeline, but omits closed-won revenue, retention, and duration. Memories 31 and 86 show durable or improved activation/adoption mechanisms, which are plausible leading indicators but do not report qualified revenue, retention, or monetization. Memory 73 reports acquisition and revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs, but omits retention, margin, customer quality, and whether promotional pricing is sustainable. Memory 91 reports only week-one engagement and first meaningful action, with no revenue, retention, or longer-horizon evidence.
